'''Oliviu Gherman''' (26 April 1930 – 11 August 2020) was a Romanian [[physicist]], [[Politics of Romania|politician]], university professor, and diplomat.

Born in 1930 in [[Mihai Viteazu, Cluj|Sânmihaiu de Sus]] village, [[Turda County]] (now part of [[Mihai Viteazu, Cluj|Mihai Viteazu]] commune, [[Cluj County]]), he completed his undergraduate studies at the [[Babeș-Bolyai University|University of Cluj]] in 1952.<ref name="bio"/> For his graduate studies, he went to the [[University of Bucharest]], where he obtained his PhD in 1957, with thesis written under the direction of [[Șerban Țițeica]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=208727}}</ref> Gherman then started his academic career at the University of Cluj, becoming dean of the Faculty of Mathematics and Physics in 1965.<ref name="bio"/> From 1958 to 1960 he worked at the [[International Atomic Energy Agency]] (IAEA) in [[Vienna]].<ref name="bio"/><ref name="md"/> In 1966 he moved to the [[University of Craiova]], where he served as department chair, dean, and [[List of academic ranks|prorector]]. In the 1970s he was a researcher, and from 1973 a senior researcher at the [[International Centre for Theoretical Physics]] in [[Trieste]].<ref name="bio">{{cite journal|first1=Radu |last1=Constantinescu|first2=Lucian|last2=Saliu|first3=György|last3=Steinbrecher|first4=Florea|last4=Uliu|url=https://rjp.nipne.ro//2010_55_9-10/0883_0887.pdf|title=In Honorem. Oliviu Gherman – 80 years old, a lifetime dedicated to Physics|journal=[[Romanian Journal of Physics]]|volume=55|issue=9–10|year=2010|pages=883–886}}</ref> He kept his faculty position in Craiova until 1998.<ref name="md"/>

After the [[Romanian Revolution]] of 1989, Gherman started on a political career. He served as a [[Senate of Romania|senator]] in the 1990–1992, 1992–1996, 1996–2000, and 2000–2004 legislatures. He was first elected in [[Dolj County]] on the lists of the [[National Salvation Front (Romania)|FSN]] party, then elected senator in the electoral constituency No. 41 of [[Bucharest]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cdep.ro/pls/parlam/structura.mp?idm=1061&cam=1&leg=1996&pag=1&idl=1|title=Oliviu Gherman. Sinteza activității parlamentare în legislatura 1996-2000|language=ro|website=www.cdep.ro|access-date=August 14, 2022|archive-date=16 March 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140316033530/http://www.cdep.ro/pls/parlam/structura.mp?idm=1061&cam=1&leg=1996&pag=1&idl=1|url-status=dead}}</ref> During his parliamentary activity, Oliviu Gherman was member of the following parliamentary friendship groups:
* in the 1990–1992 legislature: the [[State of Israel]] and the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland;
* in the 1996–2000 legislature: [[Republic of Ivory Coast]] and [[Republic of South Africa]];
* in the 2000–2004 legislature: India and [[Republic of South Africa]].

In the legislature 1996–2000, Gherman was a member of the commission for privatization and administration of state assets (since September 1999), the commission for culture, art and mass media (since December 1996) and the Committee on Labor, Family and Social Protection (until September 1999).
Gherman was the president of the [[Democratic National Salvation Front|FDSN]] party (later [[Social Democratic Party (Romania)|PDSR]]), during 1992–1996.

In 1995, Gherman was conferred a [[Honorary degree|Doctor honoris causa]] degree by the [[Moldova State University]].<ref name="bio"/><ref name="md">{{cite journal|first=Florea|last=Uliu|url=https://ibn.idsi.md/sites/default/files/imag_file/118-122_25.pdf|title=Ne-a părăsit Prof. Univ. Dr. Gherman Oliviu (26 Aprilie 1930 – 11 August 2020), o mare personalitate a fizicii din România, Doctor Honoris Causa al Universității de Stat din Republica Moldova|language=ro|journal=Fizica și Tehnologiile Moderne|volume=18|issue=3–4|year=2020|pages=118–122}}</ref>

Gherman resigned from the Senate on 27 August 2001 and was replaced by {{ill|Constantin Alexa|ro}}. Gherman was a F.S.N. senator. (1990–1992), F.D.S.N. (1992–1996), P.D.S.R. (1996–2000, 2000–2004), president of the F.D.S.N. (1992–1996), and [[President of the Senate of Romania|President of the Senate]] (1992–1996). From 2001 to 2004, Gherman was ambassador of Romania to France.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://cis01.central.ucv.ro/pauc/vol/2005_15_part2/Gherman-anniversary.pdf|title=Professor Oliviu Gherman on his 75th anniversary|website=cis01.central.ucv.ro|year=2005|access-date=August 22, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://ziare.com/basescu/presedinte/ambasadorul-romaniei-in-franta-rechemat-in-tara-73332|title=Ambasadorul României în Franța, rechemat în țară|language=ro|website=ziare.com|date=March 12, 2007|access-date=August 22, 2022}}</ref>

He died on 11 August 2020 at the age of 90.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://stirileprotv.ro/stiri/actualitate/a-murit-fostul-presedinte-al-senatului-oliviu-gherman-anuntul-facut-de-adrian-nastase.html|title=A murit fostul președinte al Senatului Oliviu Gherman. Anunțul făcut de Adrian Năstase|language=ro|website=stirileprotv.ro|date=August 11, 2020|access-date=August 14, 2022}}</ref>
